scenes.paragraphMeaning: Mio and Sōta travel from town toward the north mountain pass, pushing their bicycles up the steep road through the cool cedar woods after riding between the rice fields.
scenes.sceneDescription: Two Japanese children push their bicycles uphill along a quiet mountain road where the rice fields give way to cedar forest; the pass rises ahead under a bright blue sky with distant white summer thunderclouds.

Scene/backdrop: a rural road north of an invented Japanese canal town in summer, leaving rice fields and entering a cool cedar forest; the mountain pass rises in the distance beneath a blue sky and tall white cumulonimbus clouds.
Subject/action: Mio and her friend Sōta, both about twelve, push their simple bicycles up the steep road. Mio has black hair in a low ponytail, an ivory short-sleeved shirt, muted sage-green skirt and brown backpack. Sōta has short dark hair, a plain blue shirt, beige shorts and a navy backpack. Keep the two children friendly and naturally proportioned. Show them before any sighting on the lower road: no shadowy figure or other person.
Style/medium: simple painted children's picture-book art matching the approved Kasa Jizō inline style: broad smooth colour areas, gentle contours, minimal surface texture, few purposeful folds and shadows, two or three depth layers and a quiet simplified background; much simpler than cover art.
Composition/framing: full-bleed 12:7 landscape. Make the children and bicycles clear readable silhouettes, with the road leading from open rice fields into dark green cedar shade.
Lighting/mood: warm summer daylight, a little exertion, calm anticipation.
Palette: warm ivory, muted teal, sage foliage, ochre fields and restrained midnight-blue shadows.
Constraints: depict only the journey described in paragraph 3, before Sōta notices anything on the road below. Japanese countryside details; no cars or traffic.
Avoid: readable writing, kanji, letters, numbers, logos, extra people, a black figure, storm rain, dramatic danger, borders, watermarks, photorealism, glossy 3D, dense texture or cover-level detail.

scenes.paragraphMeaning: At the old teahouse on the pass, Mio tells the white-bearded owner her name; he stops fanning himself and recognises her as Takagi’s granddaughter.
scenes.sceneDescription: At a small wooden Japanese mountain teahouse, white-bearded Gen-san sits on the front bench with his fan paused as Mio and Sōta arrive with their bicycles; the shop sign is present but blank and unreadable.

scenes.paragraphMeaning: A sudden summer storm traps Mio and Sōta at the teahouse; Gen-san lets them inside and points out the old telephone so they can call home later.
scenes.sceneDescription: Inside the quiet old teahouse, Mio and Sōta sit safely by a window while rain veils the cedar trees; Gen-san gestures toward a simple old corded telephone. No stranger has arrived yet.
